key_insight: A physics-informed, latent-regularized U-Net can segment pathological muscle MRI accurately with much less manual labeling than conventional approaches.
clinical_relevance: This could help create patient-specific musculoskeletal segmentations for cerebral palsy and related conditions while reducing the burden of expert annotation.
method: Transfer learned from healthy MRI to improve data efficiency.
Added latent-space anatomical regularization to preserve plausible anatomy.
Used physics-informed loss terms to enforce mechanical equilibrium, near-incompressibility, and smooth deformation fields.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on MRI from 50 participants with cerebral palsy across 15 lower-limb structures, with Dice scores of 0.750 to 0.943 and ablations showing the physics-informed component contributed most to performance.
watch_item: Results come from a relatively small, disease-specific dataset, so broader validation is needed before general use.
paper_title: 3D Segmentation of Pathological Muscle with a Physics-Informed Latent-Regularized U-Net
